skill.name: design-guide
skill.description: Paperclip design system guidance for building consistent React UI components, pages, and frontend patterns using Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Radix UI, and shared component conventions.
skill.summary: Guides agents through Paperclip UI tokens, components, layouts, and design guide upkeep.
skill.author: getpaperclipai

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced TSX examples, Tailwind class examples, and headings. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, command execution, or system reconnaissance in the reviewed skill files.

content.value_statement: Paperclip frontend work can drift when components, tokens, and layout rules are not reused. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through established UI patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Paperclip design principles for dense, keyboard-first, dark-themed interfaces.
Lists the expected React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Radix UI, Lucide, and CVA stack.
Documents tokens for colors, radius, shadows, and typography.
Defines status, priority, entity row, metric card, progress bar, layout, and log viewer patterns.
Points agents to the component inventory and design guide page update rules.
limitations: It is focused on Paperclip UI, not a general design system generator.
It provides guidance, not runnable components or automated visual tests.
It assumes the repository uses the documented React and Tailwind stack.
It does not cover backend, data modeling, or security architecture.

use_cases.title: Create Consistent Components
use_cases.description: Use the documented tokens, component hierarchy, and interaction patterns before adding a reusable Paperclip UI component.

use_cases.title: Review UI Conventions
use_cases.description: Check how typography, status colors, priority icons, and layout zones should appear across Paperclip views.

use_cases.title: Modify Paperclip Pages Safely
use_cases.description: Follow page composition rules, file conventions, and design guide update requirements during frontend changes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Existing Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a small UI change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Paperclip design guide to update this UI element. Reuse existing tokens, typography, and component patterns. Explain which pattern you applied.

prompt_templates.title: Design a New Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for a reusable component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Paperclip UI component for this feature. Follow the component hierarchy, naming conventions, variants, states, and design token rules from the design guide.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Page and Showcase
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task that affects a page and documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Modify this Paperclip page using the layout and composition patterns. Update the design guide page and component index if the change adds or changes a reusable pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Feature for Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Paperclip frontend feature against the design guide. Identify mismatched tokens, typography, component choices, layout issues, and missing design guide updates.

output_examples.input: A new issue list row needs status, priority, title, assignee, and a trailing badge.
output_examples.output: The response recommends the EntityRow pattern with StatusIcon and PriorityIcon in the leading slot, a compact title, assignee subtitle, and StatusBadge trailing.

output_examples.input: A dashboard needs four summary metrics for agents, goals, issues, and spend.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a responsive MetricCard grid, semantic tokens, compact labels, minimal shadows, and no custom one-off card styling.

output_examples.input: A new reusable selector component is added to a detail page.
output_examples.output: The response includes component placement, naming guidance, design guide showcase updates, and component index documentation updates.

best_practices: Start with existing shadcn/ui primitives and Paperclip composites before creating new components.
Use semantic design tokens for colors, spacing, borders, and focus states.
Update the design guide page and component index when reusable patterns change.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode status colors or raw light and dark values.
Do not invent typography scales or page-specific visual rules.
Do not add reusable components without documenting their variants and states.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents build and review Paperclip frontend UI using the project design system.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate finished components automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and implementation guidance that an agent applies while editing the repository.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when creating components, changing pages, styling UI, or reviewing frontend consistency.

faq.question: Does it include a component inventory?
faq.answer: Yes. It references a component index with primitives, custom components, layout components, forms, and utilities.

faq.question: What should happen after adding a reusable component?
faq.answer: Update the component index and the design guide page with variants, sizes, and states.
